Figure 2:Overview ofA2D. A student-initialized synthesizer is optimized using learning-value signals from a frozen student–teacher pair. The generated questions are filtered and deduplicated into a prompt-only synthetic bank, which is then used for on-policy distillation with a frozen teacher providing supervision on the student’s top-KKcandidates.

Figure 6:Simple prompts can elicit dense distillation signals.Comparison of (a) a real question from DAPO-17k-Math and (b) a synthetic question generated by our method. Darker token backgrounds indicate higher support-aware scoressts_{t}; the strips summarize the complete rollouts, with boxes marking the displayed excerpts. Although both student answers are incorrect, the apparently simpler synthetic question elicits a higher meansts_{t}(0.172 versus 0.117; approximately1.5×1.5\times) with a shorter rollout (1,241 versus 2,002 tokens), illustrating that surface complexity alone does not characterize the density of elicited supervision.
